title: Product
description: A product in the catalog with variants and options.

id.description: Global ID (GID) uniquely identifying this product.

handle.description: URL-safe slug for SEO-friendly URLs (e.g., 'blue-runner-pro'). Use id for stable API references.

description.description: Product description in one or more formats.

categories.description: Product categories with optional taxonomy identifiers.

price_range.description: Price range across all variants. [PROPOSED: when one or more variants do not carry a range-eligible price in this response (see Variant `pricing`), `price_range` MAY be omitted; when present it MUST be computed only over the variants that carry a range-eligible price in this response — never zero-filled or synthesized for unpriced/ineligible variants (for example, variants priced $100, quote_required (no price), and $150 yield a range of $100–$150, never $0–$150) — and the product SHOULD carry a `price_on_request` disclosure warning. When no variant carries a range-eligible price, `price_range` MUST be omitted. A range-eligible price is a numeric `price` whose pricing semantics the Platform understands as usable for this caller: `pricing` absent + `price` is eligible; `mode: public` + `price` is eligible; `mode: buyer_specific` + `price` is eligible for this caller; `mode: quote_required` and `mode: contract_only` are never eligible (no price exists on the variant in either case); a variant carrying an unrecognized/unknown `pricing.mode` alongside a numeric `price` is NOT eligible to a Platform that does not understand that mode — JSON Schema cannot verify which modes a given Platform understands, so this is a behavioral producer/consumer rule, not a schema constraint. The core well-known range calculation (producer side) includes ordinary/public prices and resolved `buyer_specific` prices only. Consumer-side fallback: if a product contains a pricing mode the Platform does not understand, the Platform MUST NOT assume `product.price_range` includes only prices that are safe for it to display — the safest old-consumer behavior is to suppress or recompute the range from variants it understands. The presence of a variant's `next_step` (e.g. `request_quote`) has no bearing on range eligibility; eligibility depends solely on `pricing.mode` and price usability. When the priced variants are `buyer_specific` and resolved for a recognized caller, the resulting `price_range` is itself caller-specific and is subject to the same cache-isolation requirement as the underlying buyer-specific prices: a Platform MUST NOT expose or reuse that `price_range` for a different caller. `list_price_range`, when present, follows the same rule.] [REVIEW REVISION] `undisclosed` is never range-eligible and must not disclose whether a hidden variant is on a confidential price list. A range that includes buyer_specific prices is itself restricted and MUST NOT be sent to an unnegotiated or unauthorized consumer. Schema validity does not prove confidentiality, arithmetic, or old-client safety.

list_price_range.description: List price range before discounts (for strikethrough display).

media.description: Product media (images, videos, 3D models). First item is the featured media for listings.

variants.description: Purchasable variants of this product. First item is the featured variant for listings.

tags.description: Product tags for categorization and search.

metadata.description: Business-defined custom data extending the standard product model.

allOf.description: [PROPOSED] `price_range` is REQUIRED when every variant carries a price with absent/public/buyer_specific mode. It MAY be omitted if a variant lacks a price or uses another mode; consumers still apply range-eligibility rules.
[PROPOSED] `price_range` MUST be omitted when no variant carries a numeric price in this response.
[PROPOSED] `list_price_range` MUST be omitted when no variant carries a numeric price in this response.
